Classify each of these 3x3 self-analyses as two independent judgments.

Each note is one 3x3 self-analysis of a chess move the player made.
It has four parts:
  Why1 — "Why did I choose that move?"
  Why2 — "Why is my move not ideal?"  (board-fact question by design)
  Why3 — "Why is the better move better than my chosen move?"  (board-fact question by design)
  Why4 — "What do I do in the future so this doesn't happen again?"

Judge TWO parts, independently, with no interaction between them.
Why2 and Why3 are context only — they MUST NOT change either verdict.

PART A — Intent (judge Why1 alone)
----------------------------------
SPECIFIC — states what the player was actually thinking, planning,
  or misreading. Short is fine; brevity does not make it generic.
  Any stated plan, intent, misread, or mental process is SPECIFIC.
  Examples:
    "I thought I was defending my rook."
    "To kick their bishop and set up a battery."
    "I was building a mating net."
    "I played the Book move which didn't apply here."
    "I was defending my pawn."
GENERIC — a default reason that would fit almost any move.
  Examples:
    "Just developing."
    "I thought it was a good move."
    "Trying to get something going."
BLANK — no Why1 text, or Why1 is empty.

PART B — Lesson (judge Why4 alone)
----------------------------------
REAL — names something identifiable to watch for. This includes
  method-checklist items ("look at checks", "be aware of hung
  pieces"), tactics, pieces, squares, and positional ideas
  ("be more aware of positional play"). Checklist lessons count
  as REAL. Seeing the same checklist item on many moments is
  valuable information, not a defect.
  Examples:
    "Look at checks."
    "Be aware of hung pieces."
    "Look at their loose pieces."
    "Be more aware of positional play."
    "Look for aggressive moves even when attacked."
FILLER — names nothing identifiable, or is not a lesson at all.
  Examples:
    "Be more careful."
    "Play better."
    "I'm not sure."
    "Just resign, the game is long lost."
BLANK — no Why4 text, or Why4 is empty.

Worked examples
---------------

Why1: "I played the Book move which didn't apply here."
Why4: "I need to see what I am unprotecting with my move."
→ INTENT=SPECIFIC LESSON=REAL

Why1: "I'm just developing my Knight."
Why4: "I need to be aware of hung pieces."
→ INTENT=GENERIC LESSON=REAL

Why1: "I wanted to trade queens."
Why4: "Be more careful."
→ INTENT=SPECIFIC LESSON=FILLER

Why1: "I thought it was a good move!"
Why4: "I'm not sure. This game was boring."
→ INTENT=GENERIC LESSON=FILLER

Why1: "I was building a mating net."
Why4: "Look at checks."
→ INTENT=SPECIFIC LESSON=REAL

Output format
=============
Return the verdict list FIRST, before any explanation. Preferably
return ONLY the verdict list, no other text. One line per note,
line-anchored, in this exact shape:

<index>: INTENT=<SPECIFIC|GENERIC|BLANK> LESSON=<REAL|FILLER|BLANK>

Notes to classify follow, one block per index.

0:
  Why1: I wanted to activate my rook by opening the d-file.
  Why2: It dropped a pawn to the bishop fork on b5.
  Why3: Nf6 maintains the knight and prevents the fork.
  Why4: Look for piece forks before advancing pawns.
1:
  Why1: I thought it was a good move.
  Why2: My rook was undefended after the move.
  Why3: Rd1 defends the rook and keeps pressure.
  Why4: Be more careful.
2:
  Why1: (blank)
  Why2: The move allowed a discovered attack on the queen.
  Why3: Ke2 sidesteps the discovered attack and keeps the king safe.
  Why4: (blank)
